date: 1853-1860 (ciphered letters undated in the catalogue except c. 18r-v, 4 Feb 1857; c. 1r-v is 1858)
title: Mélanie Double (Mme Libri) to her husband Guglielmo Libri in exile: four letters with ciphered passages, names replaced by numbers
correspondents: Mélanie Double (Madame Libri, Paris) -> Guglielmo Libri (Bath/London)
shelfmark: Firenze, Biblioteca Moreniana, Palagi Libri 432 ins. 64 (CNMD 0000173096), cc. 1r-v, 9r-v, 11r-v, 18r-v
folio_note: Manus item-level notes: c. 1r-v (1858) 'Parte della lettera è crittografata'; c. 9r-v 'Alcune righe sono crittografate'; c. 11r-v 'Alcune righe sono crittografate'; c. 18r-v (4 Feb 1857) 'L'ultima parte della lettera è cifrata; nel testo alcuni nomi di persona sono indicati con numeri'. The insert holds 22 letters in French and English.
status: Manus Online (ICCU) describes the passages as ciphered ('crittografata', 'cifrata'); no decipherment or edition found. Private code between husband and wife while Libri, convicted in absentia in 1850 for the theft of manuscripts from French libraries, lived in England; the code replaces personal names by numbers and enciphers the end of the letter. The same fund (Carte Libri 9, cc. 37r-38v, 1821-1830 est.) carries marginal notes 'scritte secondo il sistema crittografico messo a punto dal Libri', so Libri used a system of his own, which may be the key.
why: 19th-century private cipher of a famous scholar-thief with several short ciphered passages in one folder, where plaintext context (the same letters in clear around the cipher, the other 18 letters, Libri's published correspondence and Maccioni Ruju-Mostert 1995) is rich; name-number codes are easy to crib. Low importance, but high solvability if the leaves are photographed.
verify: Order photographs of Palagi Libri 432 ins. 64 cc. 1, 9, 11, 18 (and Carte Libri 9 cc. 37-38 for Libri's own system) from the Biblioteca Moreniana; check Maccioni Ruju and Mostert, The Life and Times of Guglielmo Libri (1995), for any discussion of the code.
